cards.text: A great Assyrian army has come to Jerusalem. The Rabshakeh, sent by the king of Assyria, has been calling out to the people on the wall that the LORD can't deliver their city, and Hezekiah, king of Judah, told them, "Do not answer him." Now Hezekiah's officials bring him the whole report, with their clothes torn.

cards.question: When Hezekiah king of Judah hears the report of the Rabshakeh's threats, he tears his clothes and puts on sackcloth.
Clothes torn and sackcloth on, where does King Hezekiah go?

cards.text: Then Hezekiah sends out Eliakim the palace administrator, Shebna the scribe and the leading priests, every one of them in sackcloth too. Friend, that is the most serious, most ITCHY parade Jerusalem has ever seen.

cards.question: Hezekiah sends his officials and the leading priests out in sackcloth. Who are they going to see?

cards.text: They bring the prophet Isaiah son of Amoz a message from Hezekiah: today is a day of distress, rebuke and disgrace. I lived in the back of a junk drawer for YEARS, friend, and even I never had a day like that.

cards.question: In his message to Isaiah, Hezekiah says Judah still has the strength to get through this day.

cards.text: Hezekiah's picture for it: children have come to the point of birth, but there's no strength to deliver them. Then he says perhaps the LORD will hear the words of the Rabshakeh, who was sent by his master to defy the living God.

cards.question: Hezekiah hopes the LORD will hear the Rabshakeh's words and ___ him for them.
Hezekiah's message ends with a request for Isaiah. What does he ask Isaiah to do for the people who still survive?

answers.text: Lift up a prayer for them
Lead them out of the city

cards.text: So Hezekiah's servants go to Isaiah. And Isaiah sends back an answer that starts with the best four words a scared king can hear: this is what the LORD says.

cards.question: The LORD tells Hezekiah to be afraid of the words he heard from the servants of the king of Assyria.
The LORD says the servants of the king of Assyria have ___ Him with their words.

cards.text: Then the LORD says He'll put a spirit in the king of Assyria, so that he will hear a rumor. Not an army, friend, a RUMOR, the world's oldest group chat about to do the heavy lifting.

cards.question: After the king of Assyria hears that rumor, what does the LORD say he'll do?
And in his own land, the LORD says, He will cause the king of Assyria to fall by the ___.

cards.text: Meanwhile, the Rabshakeh hears that the king of Assyria has left Lachish. So he withdraws and goes looking for his boss, like somebody who just found out the meeting moved to another floor.

cards.question: The Rabshakeh finds the king of Assyria fighting against ___.

cards.text: That king is Sennacherib, king of Assyria, and he gets a warning that Tirhakah king of Cush has set out to fight against him. A second fight headed his way, and here I am losing my whole MIND when two oven timers go off at once.

cards.question: Warned that Tirhakah king of Cush is coming to fight him, what does Sennacherib do?

answers.text: Sends his army back to Lachish

cards.question: Sennacherib's message warns Hezekiah king of Judah not to let his ___ deceive him about ___.

cards.text: Then Sennacherib brags about what the kings of Assyria have done to all the other countries. He lists gods and kings by name, Gozan, Haran, Rezeph, Hamath, Arpad, Hena, Ivvah, like he's taking ATTENDANCE.

cards.question: Sennacherib asks whether the gods of the nations his fathers destroyed rescued them. What point is he making to Hezekiah?

answers.text: Your God won't rescue you either
Your God is stronger than theirs
Your God is welcome in Assyria

cards.text: Hezekiah receives the letter from the messengers and reads it. Now watch what he does with it, friend.

cards.question: After reading Sennacherib's letter, Hezekiah goes up to the house of the LORD and spreads it out before the LORD.

cards.text: No forwarding it to fifty people, no angry reply-all. Hezekiah prays, and he starts with who God is: the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel, enthroned above the cherubim, who made the heavens and the earth.

cards.question: In his prayer, Hezekiah calls the LORD one god among many over the kingdoms of the earth.
Hezekiah asks the LORD to open His ears and eyes to all the words Sennacherib sent to ___ the living God.

cards.text: Then Hezekiah admits it straight up: "Truly, O LORD, the kings of Assyria have laid waste all these countries and their lands." No spin, just the truth, laid out before the LORD.

cards.question: Hezekiah says the Assyrians threw those nations' gods into the fire and destroyed them. How could they?

answers.text: They were only wood and stone

cards.text: Then comes the big ask. Hezekiah prays, "And now, O LORD our God, save us from his hand," and he gives the LORD a reason.

cards.question: Hezekiah asks the LORD to save Judah from Sennacherib's hand. Why?

answers.text: So all kingdoms know He alone is God
So Judah can rule over Assyria
So Hezekiah can keep his throne

cards.text: And that's where we'll leave it for now. Stick close, friend, because this story is FAR from done.

findings.problem: The card cites Isaiah 36:2-37:1, but it tells nothing from 37:1. It stops at the officials bringing the report with their clothes torn (36:22). Hezekiah's response in 37:1 is held back for cards 2 and 3, so the citation runs one verse too wide. It should end at Isaiah 36:22.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The card says Isaiah's answer "starts with the best four words a scared king can hear: this is what the LORD says." That phrase is six words, not four. Isaiah's reply also doesn't start with it. It starts "Tell your master that this is what the LORD says" (Isaiah 37:6).

rule.text: What he points out must be true. "Same words" means an exact match.

findings.problem: "The world's oldest group chat" turns the rumor itself into a group chat. That blends the modern comparison into the Bible scene instead of keeping it a separate image.

rule.text: One image only. Never blend the comparison with the Bible setting.

findings.problem: The card says Sennacherib "lists gods and kings by name, Gozan, Haran, Rezeph, Hamath, Arpad, Hena, Ivvah." Those are places, not the names of gods or kings. The text says "the gods of Gozan, Haran, and Rezeph" and "the kings of Hamath, Arpad..." (Isaiah 37:12-13). The card also presents the list as his list but leaves out Eden in Telassar and Sepharvaim.

rule.text: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: "No forwarding it to fifty people, no angry reply-all" puts modern email actions into Hezekiah's scene. The comparison is blended into the Bible setting instead of standing as its own image.

rule.text: One image only. Never blend the comparison with the Bible setting.

findings.problem: The blank asks for "defy" in "sent to ___ the living God" (Isaiah 37:17). The same phrase first appears in Isaiah 37:4, and stop 1 card 8 already told the baker the Rabshakeh was sent "to defy the living God." The repeated line is asked about the second time it appears, and the earlier card gives the answer away.

rule.text: When a line repeats, like a psalm's refrain, ask about it only the first time it appears.

findings.problem: The question says Hezekiah asks the LORD "to open His ears and eyes." The text says "Incline Your ear, O LORD, and hear; open Your eyes" (Isaiah 37:17). The ears are inclined, not opened.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: The story-isn't-over line copies the doc's example word for word: "And that's where we'll leave it for now." It should be the card's own line.

rule.text: The examples show the idea. Write your own line each time.

findings.problem: This last story card is only the story-isn't-over line. It tells no verse, but it cites Isaiah 37:20. The docs allow a card that is "just this line," but they don't say what a card that tells no verse should cite.
findings.question: When the last story card is only the story-isn't-over line, what should its verses field cite: the passage's last verse, the last verse of the stop, or something else?
